catalog_quote: ... contraste d'intensité syllabi- que, comme en mbay - Moïssala ou en sara madjingay . A côté de dissyllabes dépourvus de contraste, de type GM / GS mādā [ mādā] “ cynocéphale ", le méré et le sara possèdent en effet des dissyl- labes dans lesquels l'intensité porte sur la seconde syllabe, ce qui a pour résultat de provoquer l'amuïssement de la voyelle de la première syllabe (CvCV): ex . GM / GS māta [ māta] " trois ", GM / GS vēlā [ vlā] " père " . Les termes qui font en surface [ CVC], pourraient être alors la réalisation de dissyllabes dans lesquels l'intensité porterait cette fois sur la première syllabe, la voyelle finale étant à son tour amuïe (CVCv): ainsi GM / GS dāmv [ dāmv] " grenier " serait phonologiquement / dāmvā /, GM / GS mān [ mān] " eau ", / mānā / . Ces trois types ne se répartissent pas également dans les deux par- lers . En méré, le 1er type (formes sans contraste syllabique) constitue 82 % des dissyllabes de structure CVCV et le 3ème type (CVCv) 17 %, dans l'hypothèse haute où tous les CVC sont considérés comme des CVCv . Le 2ème type (CvCV) n'est attesté que dans huit termes (dont 4 numéraux): mātá " trois ”, məká “ six ”, mandé " sept ”, ndētá " huit (GMM) ”, mvòrà bambou ... [...] Le 3ème type (CvCV) est également attesté dans les parlers koto et zura, et dans des proportions comparables au GM . En koto, par exemple, sept termes relèvent de ce type, dont trois numéraux: [running foot: Phonologie 41]

new_statements.quote: Le gula koto – langue a quatre hauteurs tonales distinctives⁶ – distingue quatre paradigmes de marques personnelles (cf. tableau 3) […] les principales différences reposant sur des contrastes d'intensité vocalique (a/Œ, i/Œ ou e/Œ) et sur des contrastes tonals. [fn. 6:] Les tons haut, moyen, bas et infra-bas sont respectivement transcrits par les diacritiques á, å, à et aˆ. Le ton infra-bas (dont aucune occurrence n'apparaît en fait dans les exemples qui nous intéressent ici) représente un développement récent de quelques-unes des langues occidentales dont la majorité oppose trois hauteurs phonologiques. [diacritics as extracted from the PDF font]
new_statements.translation: Gula Koto – a language with four distinctive tone heights – distinguishes four paradigms of person markers (cf. table 3) […] the main differences resting on contrasts of vowel intensity (a/ə, i/ə or e/ə) and on tonal contrasts. [fn. 6:] The high, mid, low and infra-low tones are transcribed respectively by the diacritics á, ā, à and a̱. The infra-low tone (of which no occurrence actually appears in the examples of interest here) represents a recent development in a few of the western languages, most of which oppose three phonological heights.

Segerer (eds), Systèmes de marques personnelles en Afrique (Afrique et Langage 8), 23-42. Louvain/Paris: Peeters. (HAL author manuscript halshs-00331347.)
new_statements.locator: HAL manuscript p. 4, §2 'Systèmes exemplaires : bongo et gula koto', subsection 'Gula koto', with footnote 6 (published pagination 23-42; exact printed page not verifiable from the manuscript)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again. File (HAL author manuscript, 21 pp., PDFLaTeX/HAL cover). extracted text gives, under the sub-heading 'Gula koto' of §2 'Systèmes exemplaires : bongo et gula koto': 'Le gula koto – langue a quatre hauteurs tonales distinctives6 – distingue quatre paradigmes de marques personnelles (cf. tableau 3), soit indépendant, indice du verbe aoriste, objet et associatif. [..] tous ces paradigmes révèlent de fortes affinités formelles, les principales différences reposant sur des contrastes d'intensité vocalique (a/Œ, i/Œ ou e/Œ) et sur des contrastes tonals.' and footnote 6: 'Les tons haut, moyen, bas et infra-bas sont respectivement transcrits par les diacritiques á,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Gula is a register-tone language: Gula Koto has four distinctive tone levels (H, M, L, infra-low), the other Gula parlers (mere, zura, sara) three (Boyeldieu & Nougayrol 2008 p. 7-8; Boyeldieu 2006). No accessible source says anything about word stress, its placement, or its absence; tone is lexically and grammatically distinctive on nouns and verbs (verb classes defined by alternating tone schemes).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any accessible source.
new_statements.exceptions: None about stress. The 2004 paper (p. 7) notes independent pronouns are 'formes accentuées' with full vowels while object/associative pronouns are enclitic with reduced vowels — a remark about pronoun prominence, not a word-stress rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the lexical tone system of Gula Koto (word level, citation forms in comparative tables); nothing on phrase-level prominence. The primary description Nougayrol 1999 was not seen and may contain an explicit 'accent' remark that would supersede this.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement concerns Gula Koto (Glottolog dialect koto1271, 'Kotoic Gula' gula1267 under gula1266); Boyeldieu & Nougayrol 2008 add that gula mere (mere1241) is a three-tone parler and that the infra-low fourth level is limited to yulu, fer and gula koto. All four parlers Nougayrol describes (koto, zura, mere, sara) fall under gula1266 (Glottolog ref 92825 language code 'Gula of Vakaga in CAR (Mere-Sara Gula-Malu-Zura-Koto de Kurbu) = Gula [kcm]'; note that record wrongly carries iso_code glu). Do not confuse with Gula (Chad) / Kulaal gula1265 [glu] or Gula Iro (Adamawa). Santandrea 1970's 'Kara' (Bubu) is filed by Glottolog under Kara [kah] kara1482 but treated as a Gula parler by Boyeldieu.

new_statements.quote: contraste d'intensité syllabique, comme en mbay-Moïssala ou en sara madjingay. A côté de dissyllabes dépourvus de contraste, de type GM/GS mādā [mādā] "cynocéphale", le méré et le sara possèdent en effet des dissyllabes dans lesquels l'intensité porte sur la seconde syllabe, ce qui a pour résultat de provoquer l'amuïssement de la voyelle de la première syllabe (CvCV) : ex. GM/GS māta [māta] "trois", GM/GS vēlā [vlā] "père". Les termes qui font en surface [CVC], pourraient être alors la réalisation de dissyllabes dans lesquels l'intensité porterait cette fois sur la première syllabe, la voyelle finale étant à son tour amuïe (CVCv)
new_statements.translation: ... a contrast of syllabic intensity, as in Mbay-Moïssala or in Sara Madjingay. Beside disyllables without any contrast, of the type GM/GS mādā [mādā] 'baboon', Méré and Sara indeed possess disyllables in which the intensity falls on the second syllable, which results in the loss of the vowel of the first syllable (CvCV): e.g. GM/GS māta [māta] 'three', GM/GS vēlā [vlā] 'father'. The words that surface as [CVC] could then be the realisation of disyllables in which the intensity would fall this time on the first syllable, the final vowel being lost in its turn (CVCv).

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog's tone-language reading and with Boyeldieu & Nougayrol 2004's mention of 'contrastes d'intensité vocalique' in Gula koto: Nougayrol 1999 adds that a lexically restricted syllabic-intensity (stress-like) contrast exists in disyllables of Méré, Sara, Koto and Zura, with the intensity on the second syllable in a closed set (CvCV) and on the first in CVCv words; no fixed placement rule.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The Gula parlers are tone languages (three tones, four in Koto: BB/MM/HM/HB schemes, 'trois tons voire plus' patterns rare), and in addition some disyllables carry a lexically determined 'contraste d'intensité syllabique' (a stress-like prominence). Three lexical types: (1) no contrast (82% of CVCV disyllables in Méré); (2) intensity on the second syllable, first vowel reduced to schwa or lost (CvCV), a closed set of eight Méré words, four of them numerals (mātá 'three', məká 'six', mandé 'seven', ndētá 'eight'), also seven words in Koto and comparable proportions in Zura; (3) intensity on the first syllable with the final vowel lost (CVCv), 17% in Méré, i.e. the surface CVC words. The weak syllable of an intensity-bearing disyllable neutralises its vowel to schwa ('Le cadre de cette neutralisation est la syllabe faible d'un dissyllabe porteur d'intensité syllabique'). So prominence is not fixed by position; it is a lexical property of a minority of disyllables, alongside distinctive tone.
new_statements.exceptions: Type 2 (second-syllable intensity) is restricted to eight Méré terms (four numerals) and seven Koto terms (three numerals); most disyllables (82% in Méré) have no intensity contrast; footnote 14: the tendency to vowel loss is weaker in Méré and Sara than elsewhere. The lexicon's conventions say that, where several tone schemes compete, the most widespread form is the headword, and one clause (context lost between snippets) states that in some cited forms 'l'accent porte sur la deuxième syllabe'.
new_statements.identity_note: Nougayrol 1999 describes the Gula parlers of the Vakaga (CAR): méré (GM), sara (GS), zura (GZ) and koto (GK), with comparisons to Gula of Sudan and Chad; the intensity passage is stated first for Méré and Sara ('le méré et le sara possèdent..') and then extended to Koto and Zura ('Le 3ème type (CvCV) est également attesté dans les parlers koto et zura'). Glottolog files the book under gula1266 = Gula [kcm] though its record carries iso_code glu (Kulaal, Chad) in one field; the Boyeldieu & Nougayrol 2004 statement concerns Gula koto specifically. Tucker & Bryan's 'Gula' identity not checked (work not opened).

It is compatible with the catalog/Nougayrol picture (tone language; in disyllables prominence on the first syllable goes with a reduced final vowel = Nougayrol's CVCv, prominence on the second with a centralised first vowel = Nougayrol's CvCV) and adds a group-level default of initial prominence in disyllables. new_statements.rule_in_words: Group-level statement for the Bongo-Bagirmi languages (whose 'Central languages' include KARA, i.e. Santandrea's Kara/'bu'bu of Kafia Kingi, treated by Boyeldieu 2006 as a Gula variety; the name 'Gula' itself does not occur in the volume's scanned): the languages are tonal (three levels) and stress in disyllables is normally initial, always initial when the second vowel is semi-mute, occasionally on the second syllable when the first vowel is central.
new_statements.exceptions: second-syllable stress when the first syllable has a central vowel (Bagirmi example from Stevenson)
new_statements.identity_note: Nougayrol 1999 describes the Gula dialect cluster of the Vakaga (CAR) and adjacent Sudan/Chad: méré (GM), sara (GS), zura (GZ), koto (GK), moto-mar, plus Santandrea's 'bu'bu/Kara (BS) data; the stress passage concerns Méré and Sara with a note that the CvCV type also occurs in Koto and Zura. Tucker & Bryan 1966 treat the Bongo-Bagirmi group; the only Gula-related lect named is KARA (Santandrea's Kara of Kafia Kingi, Glottolog kara1482, counted as a Gula variety by Boyeldieu 2006); 'Gula' does not occur in the scanned. Not to be confused with Gula Iro / Bon Gula (Adamawa, Chad).

tone_statements.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2009. Le quatrième ton du yulu. Journal of African Languages and Linguistics 30(2): 193-230. Berlin: Walter de Gruyter. DOI 10.1515/jall.2009.009. (HAL author manuscript halshs-00348143, 31 pp; the HAL record and the manuscript's cover sheet give the pages as 197-234, the publisher's metadata as 193-230.)
tone_statements.quote: 6.1. Les tons du fer et du gula koto. Deux langues historiquement et géographiquement proches du yulu, le fer et le gula koto, connaissent elles-mêmes quatre hauteurs tonales. Les systèmes de ces langues, tous deux très semblables de ce point de vue, se distinguent toutefois du système yulu en ce que le ton infra-bas (0) y apparaît essentiellement dans des schèmes contrastés (hétérotones), majoritairement représentés par le schème 10 [...] Les consonnes sonores n'ont en effet joué aucun rôle dans le développement du registre infra-bas de ces langues dont le schème 10 résulte de la transposition globale vers le bas d'un schème originel SBB *21, transposition vraisemblablement favorisée, sinon nécessitée, par la confusion concomitante des réflexes respectifs des schèmes *11 et *12 en 11 [...] Nougayrol (1999 : 44-45), sensible à l'argument, plaide toutefois pour une analyse phonologique du registre infra-bas et du schème BiB (10) du gula koto qui peut seule expliquer l'identité tonale des parlers voisins que constituent le gula méré et le gula sara, lesquels ont un temps partagé le même système avant de revenir à une distinction de trois hauteurs, mais avec des schèmes distincts des…
tone_statements.translation: 6.1. The tones of Fer and Gula Koto. Two languages historically and geographically close to Yulu, Fer and Gula Koto, themselves have four tone heights. The systems of these languages, both very similar in this respect, nevertheless differ from the Yulu system in that the infra-low tone (0) appears there essentially in contrastive (heterotone) schemes, mostly represented by the scheme 10 [...] Voiced consonants in fact played no role in the development of the infra-low register of these languages, whose scheme 10 results from the global downward transposition of an original SBB scheme *21, a transposition probably favoured, if not required, by the concomitant merger of the respective reflexes of schemes *11 and *12 as 11 [...] Nougayrol (1999: 44-45), receptive to the argument, nevertheless argues for a phonological analysis of the infra-low register and of the Infra-low-Low (10) scheme of Gula Koto, which alone can explain the tonal identity of the neighbouring lects Gula Mere and Gula Sara, which for a time shared the same system before returning to a distinction of three heights, but with schemes distinct from the original ones.
tone_statements.locator: HAL manuscript halshs-00348143, section 6.1 'Les tons du fer et du gula koto', ms p. 21 (opening paragraph) and pp. 21-22 (status of the infra-low); Annexe tableau 1 header, ms p. 28
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Register-tone system. Gula koto: four level tones (infra-low, low, mid, high), the infra-low being marginal and largely confined to the Infra-low+Low (10) word scheme, historically *21 shifted down; gula méré and gula sara: three level tones (low, mid, high). No stress content in this work.

tone.translation: 6.1. The tones of Fer and Gula Koto. Two languages historically and geographically close to Yulu, Fer and Gula Koto, themselves have four tone heights. The systems of these languages, both very similar in this respect, nevertheless differ from the Yulu system in that the infra-low tone (0) appears there essentially in contrastive (heterotone) schemes, mostly represented by the scheme 10 [...] Voiced consonants in fact played no role in the development of the infra-low register of these languages, whose scheme 10 results from the global downward transposition of an original SBB scheme *21, a transposition probably favoured, if not required, by the concomitant merger of the respective reflexes of schemes *11 and *12 as 11 [...] Nougayrol (1999: 44-45), receptive to the argument, nevertheless argues for a phonological analysis of the infra-low register and of the Infra-low-Low (10) scheme of Gula Koto, which alone can explain the tonal identity of the neighbouring lects Gula Mere and Gula Sara, which for a time shared the same system before returning to a distinction of three heights, but with schemes distinct from the original ones.

tone.summary: Register-tone system. Gula koto: four level tones (infra-low, low, mid, high), the infra-low being marginal and largely confined to the Infra-low+Low (10) word scheme, historically *21 shifted down; gula méré and gula sara: three level tones (low, mid, high). No stress content in this work.
